newsitem.title: NORWAY: Kvaerner says wins China bridge contract.
newsitem.headline: Kvaerner says wins China bridge contract.

text.p: Kvaerner Cleveland Bridge Ltd, a British subsidiary of Norway's Kvaerner ASA, has won a contract worth more than 100 million stg to build a steel-suspension bridge over the Yangtze River in China, Kvaerner said on Monday.
Kvaerner's London headquarters, confirming a report in the Financial Times, said in a statement the contract involved building the fourth longest single-span suspension bridge in the world.
It said the contract was signed on Monday by Managing Director Jeremy Beeton in Lancaster House, London.

"There is a significant long term market for major bridges in China and this will allow us to expand and further develop our engineering expertise, as well as develop long term business relationships with local Chinese companies for targeting future projects," Beeton was quoted as saying.

The British Government, through its Overseas Development Administration (ODA) and Export Credits Guarantee Department (ECGD) is supporting the contract with a concessional loan to cover the full value of the UK goods and services amounting to approximately 55 million stg.
